title.en: Partitive examples: shopping / in a café / in a bar

summary: English sentences to translate into Finnish when shopping for food, ordering in a café and in a bar, practising the partitive after numbers and measure words.
transcript:
OSTOKSILLA= DOING SHOPPING

One small salmon, please.

Two perches, please. (AHVEN= PERCH)

Two large perches, please.

A piece of Dutch cheese, please.

Two small tubs of salad, please. (TUB= PURKKI, SALAD= SALAATTI)

Half a kilo of mincemeat. (PUOLI= HALF, KILO= KILO, JAUHELIHA= MINCEMEAT)

Two fresh wholemeal breads. (WHOLEMEAL BREAD=TÄYSJYVÄLEIPÄ)

Three packets of coffee and one 1,5 kilos of sausage. (PACKET= PAKETTI, ONE AND A HALF= PUOLITOISTA)

KAHVILASSA = IN A COFFEE SHOP

Two glasses of water, please.

Four warm Karelian pies, please.

Two Cokes (kokis) and two meat pies, please.

Two small black coffees, one large latte and three pieces of cheese cake, please. (LATTE=LATTE)

Two large coffees, a glass of water, a glass of oeange juice and two cheese sandwiches, please.

Three chicken salads, two glasses of white wine and some salad dressing, please.
(CHICKEN= KANA, SALAD DRESSING= SALAATTIKASTIKE)

One green salad, two plates of salmon soup, a large glass of milk and two glasses of water, please.
(GREEN SALAD= VIHERSALAATTI, PLATE= LAUTANEN, SALMON SOUP= LOHIKEITTO)

BAARISSA

Glass of orange juice, please.

One Aperol Spritz and two small glasses of red wine.

A bottle of Australian wine and two beers, please. (AUSTRALIA= AUSTRALIA)

Three cans of Lapin Kulta (Finnish beer brand), please. (CAN= TÖLKKI)

Three large pints of German beer and a glass of water, please. (PINT= TUOPPI)

Two large glasses of sparkling wine and the bill, please. (BILL= LASKU)
